detail: Fed funds lifted from 1.00%; 17 consecutive 25bp hikes to 5.25% by mid-2006.

event: China drops the yuan's dollar peg
detail: PBoC revalues the yuan ~2% and moves to a managed float; dollar-bloc repricing.
Shanghai Composite -9% triggers a worldwide equity drop; first tremor of the credit cycle.
Bank halts redemptions citing an inability to value subprime paper; money markets seize.

event: Fed's first cut of the crisis
detail: FOMC cuts 50bp to 4.75% as the credit crunch spreads.
JPMorgan buys Bear Stearns with Fed backstop; first systemic domino.
WTI hits its all-time intraday high before collapsing into year-end.
Largest bankruptcy in US history; global funding markets freeze, flight to safety.
$700bn US bank-rescue package enacted amid the panic.
Fed begins large-scale asset purchases (initially agency MBS).
S&P 500 closes at 676, the post-crisis low; risk assets begin a multi-year rally.
FOMC adds $300bn of long-term Treasury buying; dollar drops, gold jumps.
EU/IMF EUR110bn package; start of the euro-area sovereign debt crisis.
$600bn Treasury purchase program; weak dollar, commodity reflation.
First-ever downgrade of US sovereign debt to AA+ after the debt-ceiling standoff.
Spot gold peaks near $1,920/oz at the height of the euro crisis and US downgrade.
Fed lengthens the maturity of its portfolio to push down long-term yields.
ECB president pledges to preserve the euro; euro-crisis risk premium collapses.
Open-ended $40bn/month MBS purchases ('QE-infinity').
Bernanke hints at slowing QE; Treasury yields spike, EM and gold sell off.
FOMC concludes asset purchases; balance sheet held steady.
OPEC holds production into a supply glut; WTI falls from ~$75 toward $26 by early 2016.
Surprise ~2% CNY devaluation triggers a global risk-off wave into late August.
First rate hike since 2006 (to 0.25-0.50%); the ZIRP era formally ends.
WTI hits its cycle low as the shale glut peaks.
UK votes to leave the EU; sterling crashes, gold and Treasuries rally.
'Reflation trade': yields and the dollar spike, gold falls into year-end.

event: Fed hikes into a falling market
detail: Fourth 2018 hike despite a sharp Q4 selloff; policy-error fears, volatility spike.
First cut since 2008 (25bp) as trade-war growth fears mount.

event: Attack on Saudi Abqaiq oil facility
detail: Drone/missile strike knocks out ~5% of world supply; oil posts its biggest one-day jump on record.

event: OPEC+ breaks down; Saudi-Russia price war
detail: Saudi Arabia slashes prices and lifts output; WTI drops ~25% on 9 March.
Global lockdowns; fastest bear market in history, cross-asset liquidation.
Open-ended purchases plus credit facilities; US equities bottom the same day.
May WTI settles at -$37.63 as storage runs out at contract expiry.

event: Gold sets a new record above $2,000
detail: Real yields deeply negative post-COVID; gold peaks near $2,075.
FOMC starts winding down pandemic QE as inflation runs hot.
Energy and commodity shock; gold and oil spike, risk-off across markets.

event: Commodities spike on the Ukraine war
detail: Brent briefly tops $130; broad commodity surge and a nickel-market blowup.
First of a run of hikes (including four 75bp moves) to fight 9% inflation.
Unfunded tax cuts crater gilts and sterling; the BoE intervenes to stop an LDI spiral.
Largest bank failure since 2008; regional-bank stress, a dash to Treasuries and gold.
Long-end yields hit their highest since 2007 on 'higher for longer' and heavy supply.
First cut of the easing cycle as inflation cools toward target.
Sweeping US tariffs announced; the total US stock market falls ~12% into 9 April, oil slides.
Country-specific tariffs paused (10% baseline kept); sharp equity rebound.

event: Gold sells off from record highs
detail: Gold drops >2% on easing US-China trade tension, a firmer dollar and rotation out of the trade.

event: Gold breaks $5,000/oz for the first time
detail: Parabolic run on record central-bank buying and tariff-driven safe-haven demand.
Gold falls ~11% from its record in days (silver >30%); the blow-off top reverses hard.

event: US and Israel begin strikes on Iran
detail: Iran closes the Strait of Hormuz; ~20% of world oil transit halts, crude spikes from ~$60 toward ~$115.
Renewed strikes keep the Hormuz shipping disruption and the oil risk premium in place.
Conflict resumes after a spring ceasefire; Iranian forces attack Gulf shipping, oil jumps again.
